question.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the limit using the algebra of limits, as follows:

$$
{lim}_{x\to {5}^{-}}(-\frac{9}{4(x-5)^{6}})\,=\,-\frac{9}{4}\,\cdot \,{lim}_{x\to {5}^{-}}\frac{1}{(x-5)^{6}}.
$$

Now, we can sketch the graph of $y=\frac{1}{(x-5)^{6}}$ as follows:

1\. Take the graph of $y=\frac{1}{{x}^{6}}.$

2\. Translate it to the right by $5$ units. This gives $y=\frac{1}{(x-5)^{6}},$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14247879/assets/574b270248f2acc2a2eb3403f5626e420f5f16abc6e9e01dcb147df83e5806b5.png)

From the graph, we see that

$$
{lim}_{x\to {5}^{-}}\frac{1}{(x-5)^{6}}=\infty .
$$

Finally, the negative factor of $-\frac{9}{4}$ changes the sign of the limit. Therefore, we conclude that

$$
-\frac{9}{4}\cdot {lim}_{x\to {5}^{-}}\frac{1}{(x-5)^{6}}=-\infty .
$$
